name: Monitoring & Alerting
description: Enforces monitoring and alerting best practices for production systems including SLOs, dashboards, and on-call.
content:
# Monitoring & Alerting Rules

- Define SLOs (Service Level Objectives) before building alerts — alert on SLO burn rate, not individual metrics
- Monitor the four golden signals — latency, traffic, errors, and saturation for every service
- Use structured logging (JSON) — include request ID, user ID, service name, and timestamp in every log entry
- Set up distributed tracing — use OpenTelemetry to trace requests across service boundaries
- Create dashboards for each service — show health at a glance with the four golden signals and business metrics
- Alert on symptoms (user impact), not causes (CPU usage) — high CPU is only a problem if it affects latency or errors
- Set meaningful alert thresholds — use historical baselines, not arbitrary numbers. Tune to reduce false positives
- Include runbooks in alert notifications — link to documentation that explains what the alert means and how to respond
- Use severity levels — P1 (pages on-call immediately), P2 (respond within hours), P3 (review next business day)
- Implement health check endpoints (`/health`, `/ready`) — separate liveness from readiness probes
- Monitor error budgets — track how much of your SLO budget is consumed and slow down releases when budget is low
- Review and prune alerts quarterly — remove noisy alerts that are ignored, fix flappy alerts that erode trust
